summary:
We developed Artemis Lunar South Pole Rover, an interactive 3D browser-based space exploration simulation built with WebGL (Three.js) and the Web Audio API. Starting with a cinematic Earth-to-Moon rocket launch sequence, players pilot a 6-wheel autonomous rover with articulated rocker-bogie suspension across procedurally generated lunar craters and boulder fields.

To address the challenges of extreme lunar environments and remote resource prospecting, the simulation integrates real-time slope telemetry, radar spectral scanning ([R]), mineral sample collection ([E]), and life-support management. Players must strategically monitor battery and oxygen reserves—docking at Artemis Oxygen Stations ([O]) to prevent hypoxia-induced motor and sensor impairment.

This project is important because it transforms complex aerospace engineering, lunar geology, and NASA/JAXA Artemis mission objectives into an accessible, zero-installation STEM learning experience that inspires future space explorers.
